content_blocks.heading: How should I wash hand-block cotton, and does this store sell bedsheets?
content_blocks.body: Wash cold or lukewarm on a gentle cycle with mild detergent, skip bleach and fabric softener, dry in the shade and iron on the reverse with steam or a light mist. That is a general cotton-care protocol drawn from comparable hand-block product labels, not a Sanskruti Homes instruction we found. On 26 Nov 2026 sanskrutihomes.in showed sleepwear, ethnic wear and home decor — not the bedsheets and dohars described in older Durza copy. We say so plainly rather than pretending the match exists.

items.title: The storefront mismatch, stated first
items.body: The site linked from this guide, sanskrutihomes.in, presented menus for Women, Kids, Men, Collections, Winter Styles, Home Decor, Pre-Order Styles and Plus Size — including night suits, kurta sets, cushion covers, throws and rugs. We found no bedsheets, dohars or kitchen towels in that navigation. A separate retailer, Sanskruti Store on sanskrutistore.com, does list hand-block printed cotton bedsheets. These may be related names, but they are different domains and we do not treat them as the same seller.

items.title: What a comparable cotton label actually says
items.body: A Sanskruti Store listing for a pure cotton hand-block printed Jaipuri bedsheet specifies 116 thread count, queen 90 × 108 inches, king 108 × 108 inches, 28 × 20 inch pillow covers, and 'Machine Wash In Cold Water'. It also notes that variation in colour and pattern is inherent to handloom products. That is the closest care evidence we could attach to the category — it is not an instruction from the linked storefront.

items.title: The cold-wash, shade-dry protocol
items.body: Use cold or lukewarm water around 30°C on a gentle cycle, with a mild detergent. Skip bleach and fabric softener, and do not tumble-dry hot. Line-dry in the shade: direct sun can bleach hand-block pigments unevenly. Iron on the reverse side with steam or a light mist. Hot ironing is tolerable for cotton, but dry-ironing directly over a print risks scorch marks and a flattened finish.

items.title: Shrink maths — shown, not promised
items.body: Older Durza copy said handspun cotton shrinks 3–5% on the first wash. We could not verify that figure from the linked store. If it holds, a 108-inch sheet loses roughly 3.2 to 5.4 inches and a 90-inch width loses about 2.7 to 4.5 inches. That is arithmetic from an unverified assumption, useful for planning but not a guarantee. The safest approach is to measure your bed, add a margin and pre-wash before any stitching.

items.title: First wash and storage
items.body: Wash a new piece once before use to remove loose surface pigment and sizing. Wash dark and light prints separately for the first few cycles. Store fully dry in a breathable cotton bag away from direct sunlight; damp folding is what creates mildew spots in a monsoon cupboard. These are general cotton-care practices, not brand-specific test results.

links.title: How we audit a product claim

items.q: Will my cotton sheet shrink after the first wash?
items.a: Some movement is normal, but we could not verify the 3–5% figure from an older Durza draft. If that rate held, a 108-inch sheet would lose roughly 3.2 to 5.4 inches. Measure your bed, allow a margin and pre-wash before stitching instead of trusting the number.

items.q: Can I iron at high heat?
items.a: Cotton tolerates a hot iron, but do it on the reverse side with steam or a light mist. Dry ironing directly on a hand-block print risks scorch marks and a flattened finish. Test on a small corner first.

items.q: What is the right wash temperature?
items.a: Cold or lukewarm, around 30°C, on a gentle cycle with mild detergent. A comparable hand-block cotton bedsheet listing publishes 'machine wash in cold water'. Avoid bleach, softener and hot tumble drying.

The linked storefront did not show bedsheets, dohars or kitchen towels in the catalogue we read on 26 Nov 2026. A different domain, sanskrutistore.com, does list hand-block cotton bedsheets. Check the URL before you buy.

items.q: Did Durza wash or test any linen?
items.a: No. We read storefronts and published care guidance and make no durability or shrinkage guarantees.
